items.summary:
수입 찾는 20대는 이거 읽어두면 첫 달 안 날림
월 40만원 벌던 25살이 월매출 1억 찍은 아마존 구매대행 5단계

군 전역 후 적금 300만원으로 시작한 대표가 직접 공개한 월매출 1억대 아마존 구매대행 운영 화면과 5단계 공정

아마존 구매대행은 10년 된 레드오션이라 마진이 안 남고, 중국 도매만 뒤지면 된다는 말을 그대로 믿으면 안 된다는 걸 알게 됨. 이분은 남들과 같은 방식이 아니라 마진 30% 이상 나오는 상품만 고르는 게 핵심이라고 말함

이분은 97년생 대표로, 군 적금 300만원으로 노트북 한 대를 사서 부모님 집에서 시작했다고 털어놓음. 처음 7개월은 하루 16~17시간씩 일하고도 순이익이 월 40만원이었다고 함. 그런데 지금은 하루 15~30분만 일한다며, 화면을 직접 새로고침해서 이번 달 매출 1억 2천만원을 보여줌. 가장 잘 나온 달은 매출 약 1억 8천만원, 마진은 30% 정도, 반품과 취소는 거의 0이라고 함 ㄷㄷ

이분이 제시한 구매대행 공정 5가지는 다음과 같음

1. 뭘 팔지 정하는 게 제일 어려움
초보가 가장 막히는 구간이 상품 고르기라고 짚음. 직접 만든 GPT 앱에 '오늘 핼러윈 상품 올릴 거야'라고 치면 아마존 베스트셀러 중 한국 취향에 맞는 걸 엑셀로 뽑아 줌. 그날 목록에는 고딕 장식, 유령 장식, 반려동물 의상이 올라옴. 재고가 없는 구조라 시즌 한 달 전이 아니라 내일부터 팔 수 있다는 점도 강조함.

2. 수집은 엑셀 넣고 버튼 하나
엑셀을 전용 프로그램에 넣으면 AI가 사진을 보고 카테고리를 알아서 맞춤. 시연 화면의 작업 기록에는 70시간 전에 돌린 수집이 21만 개를 모아 둔 상태였음. 예전엔 하루 3~10개 올렸는데 지금은 6만 개까지 올린다고 함.

3. 올리기 전에 팔리게 가공하기
번역된 상품명은 길고 어색해서, 'AI 상품 번역'을 누르면 한국 감각에 맞게 줄이고 네이버 글자 수 기준에도 맞춤. 상세페이지보다 클릭이 먼저라서 상품명과 태그로 노출 순위를 올리는 데 공을 들인다고 함.

4. 등록은 여섯 번 클릭
키보드를 치워 놓고 마우스로 여섯 번 눌러 스마트스토어와 쿠팡에 올리는 걸 보여줌. 찾기, 수집, 가공, 등록 네 단계가 이 안에서 끝남.

5. 주문은 아마존이 배송까지
주문이 들어오면 아마존 주소를 영어로 넣고 구매 버튼만 누르면 아마존이 배송을 하고 반품도 받아 줌. 고객 문의는 하루 3~4건 수준이고 이것도 AI가 맡는다고 함. 그래서 하루 15~30분이 가능하다는 설명임.

진짜 이런 거 보면 '자동화 프로그램'보다 '뭘 팔지 고르는 감각과 7개월 버틴 시간'이 필요한 이유가 있는듯. 매출 1억은 순이익이 아니라 마진 30% 기준으로 봐야 하고, 이 프로그램은 수강생 전용에 서버·개발비가 월 20만원이라 구독자에게는 1주일만 열어 준다고 했음. 영상 끝은 단톡방 가입 유도라 홍보 성격이 있고 수강생 성과도 개인별 사례일 뿐이라는 점은 걸러 봐야 함. 사업자 등록과 통관 같은 규정도 따로 확인해야 함

자동화는 맨 마지막에 오는 거구나 싶음

items.title: My First Impressions of Fable 5.2
items.summary:
My First Impressions of Fable 5.2

I’ve been using it for a few hours now, and I have a few thoughts on the new Fable 5.2:

1. The weirdest RL I've ever seen. On some tasks it's a genius; on others, it's as dumb as a shrimp. In pure coding tasks, it's at least on par with Opus 5.5. But ask it to reason through something non-standard that isn't coding-related, and its output drops to the level of GPT-3.5. I asked both Fable 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra to flesh out a project idea and Fable’s response was complete garbage

2.  Fable models have always been notorious for mediocre taste - worse than Opus. This time, Fable surprised me with a complete absence of it. In a long list, it inexplicably added two separate pagination controls: one expands the currently loaded list of data, and the second one underneath fetches new content. On top of that, you can see plenty of demos on X with pretty mediocre results that are even worse than Opus

3. It seems to be the most token-hungry model in the world. The advertised price cut makes zero sense when Fable 5.2 burns through four times more tokens than 5.1

4. The most pedantic model yet. It constantly tries to prove you wrong. Tell it that snow is white, and it will find a million reasons why that's not entirely accurate. GPT-6 Astra had this annoying trait as well

5. It’s noticeably faster. On medium effort, it responds almost instantaneously

6. Fable 5.5 has picked up a trait that used to belong to Sonnet 5.5 - diligence. Once it takes on a task, it will check and iterate multiple times until it achieves a solid result

7. For coding tasks, there is zero difference compared to Opus 5.5. Across all other aspects, Opus 5.5 is, in my subjective view, superior to Fable 5.5

I’ve never really liked Fable models. There’s not much point to them. They’re stubborn, weighed down by guardrail filters, have poor taste, and are expensive, token-hungry, and in some areas worse than the Opus lineup. This one is no exception. In my view, the new Fable 5.2 makes no sense, and I think I understand why they called this release 5.2 rather than 5.5. A revolutionary leap like the jump from Opus 5 to 5.5 just didn't happen

items.title: Larry Page figured out something most ambitious people never do:
items.summary:
Larry Page figured out something most ambitious people never do:

"It is often easier to make progress on mega-ambitious dreams. Since no one else is crazy enough to do it, you have little competition."

Think about what this actually means mechanically:

When you pursue a "reasonable" idea, you're competing against hundreds of founders who saw the same opportunity, dozens of VCs who've already built a mental model of what success looks like, and a market that benchmarks you daily.

When you pursue something nobody believes is possible, the competitive field is almost empty. Investors don't know what failure looks like either — which buys you time. And the category doesn't exist yet, so you get to define it.

Google didn't try to build a slightly better search engine. Page and Brin wanted to index all of human knowledge. That audacity wasn't a liability — it was a moat before they had a product.

The same logic applies to SpaceX (reusable rockets were "obviously" impossible), to Stripe (payments were "solved"), to OpenAI circa 2015 (AGI research was considered academic theater).

The most crowded space in startups is the middle: ambitious enough to be interesting, safe enough to feel rational. That's where competition is brutal and differentiation is marginal.

Page's insight is a competitive strategy, not an inspiration poster. If everyone else has filtered out the crazy idea, the field is yours.

items.title: building a game with claude opus 5.5 + godot..
items.summary:
building a game with claude opus 5.5 + godot..

nightshoal: a 1920s sailing and fishing game with home islands

the trick is letting opus build, and giving it tools to judge itself. here’s the workflow:

- step 1: opus 5.5 in claude code writes all the code and builds the city layout and buildings in blender via mcp
- step 2: for complex models: make one image with 4 sides (front, back, left, right), opus splits it into 4, upload all 4 to tripo
- step 3: opus fixes tripo models in blender via mcp, and keeps tripo’s textures or makes its own to fit the style
- step 4: generate mockups with the openai image api (6 views x 4 times of day = 24)
- step 5: run a “gauntlet loop”: critic agents compare the game against the mockups blind. a piece that wins twice is done
- step 6: build an in-game performance panel, then have opus scan the whole game and report what costs the most
- step 7: let jev pick the effort level for every task (perf fixes got “extra,” the full scan got max)

who does what:

> opus 5.5: all code, blender buildings, perf fixes, even the video edit
> tripo: ships, warehouses, piers, rods
> openai image api: the mockups the critics judge against
> jev: effort levels and trailer direction
> godot: the engine

loops can’t delete what the game already has. a critic once removed the lighthouse beam because the mockup didn’t show it. (dev: RUSuper)

Andrej Karpathy:

“A 1B model can be much more effective than most current LLMs.

90% of current models waste a ton of capacity and money on remembering stuff that doesn’t matter.”

here is his 5 core thesis about Small LLM’s:

1. the intelligence was never the knowledge. Strip the memorized internet, keep the reasoning. What’s left is the cognitive core, and it’s small.

2. the core might fit in ~1B params. Maybe less. “Plenty of room at the bottom.” We’ve been paying for a library when we needed a brain.

3. size stopped being the bottleneck. What makes an agent work is the tools it can call and how tight the feedback loop is, not parameter count.

4. intelligence lives in the system, not the weights. A raw LLM is a CPU with no OS. Small core + good harness > giant model alone.

5. you can own it. A model on your hardware is one no one can rate-limit, price-hike, or deprecate on you.

in 12 months the gap between teams shipping on-device and teams paying per-token frontier bills won’t be capability.

TwIL an 8.8B model at 90%+ of frontier isn’t a benchmark flex.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy.
    
    Args:
        n: Vị trí trong dãy Fibonacci (bắt đầu từ 0)
        
    Returns:
        Số Fibonacci tại vị trí n
    """
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    else:
        return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Ví dụ sử dụng
if __name__ == "__main__":
    for i in range(10):
        print(f"F({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

**Kết quả:**
```
F(0) = 0
F(1) = 1
F(2) = 1
F(3) = 2
F(4) = 3
F(5) = 5
F(6) = 8
F(7) = 13
F(8) = 21
F(9) = 34
```

---

⚠️ **Lưu ý:** Cách này có độ phức tạp thời gian **O(2ⁿ)** do tính toán lặp lại nhiều lần. Với `n` lớn (>35), sẽ rất chậm.

**Phiên bản tối ưu hơn (memoization):**
```python
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def fibonacci(n):
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)
```

Hoặc dùng **iterative** (O(n) time, O(1) space):
```python
def fibonacci(n):
    a, b = 0, 1
    for _ in range(n):
        a, b = b, a + b
    return a
```

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
